definitions.explanation: A state of deep distress or painful difficulty when facing a hard decision or situation. Often describes the tortured deliberation involved in making an unpleasant choice.

examples.japanese: {苦渋|くじゅう}の{決断|けつだん}を{下|くだ}した。
{社長|しゃちょう}は{苦渋|くじゅう}の{表情|ひょうじょう}でリストラを{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: The president announced the layoffs with a pained expression.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{続|つづ}けてきた{事業|じぎょう}を{閉|し}めるという{苦渋|くじゅう}の{選択|せんたく}を{迫|せま}られた。
examples.english: I was forced to make the painful choice of closing a business I had run for many years.

notes:
A compound of {苦|く} (bitterness, suffering) and {渋|じゅう} (astringent, reluctant). The two characters together evoke something deeply unpleasant to endure.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苦渋|くじゅう}の{決断|けつだん} (agonizing decision)
- {苦渋|くじゅう}の{選択|せんたく} (painful choice)
- {苦渋|くじゅう}の{表情|ひょうじょう} (anguished expression)
- {苦渋|くじゅう}に{満|み}ちた (filled with anguish)

Very commonly appears in the set phrase {苦渋|くじゅう}の{決断|けつだん}, which is a staple of news reports and political speech. Implies that the decision was reached only after much painful deliberation and is not one the speaker wanted to make.
